title: Federal Judge Dismisses GAP Coverage Lawsuit
summary: Trade-press report on a court dismissing a class action that called a dealer group's GAP coverage phony.

assertions.quote: the consumer could get less money than the total remaining loan balance

verdicts.note: Court records in this case confirm the payout formula can leave a shortfall versus the full loan balance, matching how GAP products are generally structured.

CFPB found servicers miscalculated GAP-waiver refunds, in one pattern resulting in underpayment to the consumer -- showing the payout can fall short in practice, though due to servicer error rather than an inherent limit on what GAP covers.

assertions.quote: Maryland dealers can't be held liable for any inconsistencies in the language of the GAP contract

verdicts.note: This reflects the actual court holding in this specific case, a narrow but real legal principle that liability turns on claims practice, not wording alone.

assertions.quote: did not suffer a loss of their vehicle

verdicts.note: This is the stated basis for the court's dismissal in the record, though it is a narrow procedural outcome, not a broad vindication of all GAP products.

assertions.quote: the value of vehicle is determined by either the insurance company or the book value of the vehicle — whichever value is higher

verdicts.note: This valuation mechanism is stated directly in the contract terms described in the court record and is a common structure in GAP products generally.
